question: I'm a sociology major going into my junior year soon, what are all the courses I still need to take for the major besides the intro ones?

body.answer:
The catalog lists the following Sociology BA major requirements besides SOCI 101 INTRODUCTION TO SOCIOLOGY. It can’t show which you personally still need without your records. [1]

Required courses: SOCI 202 SOCIAL INEQUALITY; SOCI 215 SOCIOLOGY OF RACE RELATIONS; SOCI 250 INTERNATIONAL MIGRATION & HUMAN RIGHTS; SOCI 302 WOMEN AND GLOBAL POVERTY or SOCI 361 GENDER, WORK, AND FAMILY; SOCI 304 GLOBALIZATION AND SOCIETY; SOCI 307 SOCIAL RESEARCH WITH COMPUTERS; SOCI 308 DATA ANALYSIS IN SOCIOLOGY; SOCI 317 SOCIOLOGY OF COMMUNITY: FIELDWORK; SOCI 332 SOCIAL THEORY; SOCI 410 CAPSTONE PROJECT IN SOCIOLOGY. [1]

Concentration requirements: Criminology requires SOCI 245 CRIMINOLOGY and at least 2 electives from SOCI 248 CRIME AND MEDIA; SOCI 255 HUMAN RIGHTS IN THE CONTEXT OF LAW ENFORCEMENT; SOCI 315 SOCIOLOGY OF DEVIANCE; SOCI 345 RACE, CRIME AND JUSTICE; SOCI 390 TOPICS. Social Inequality requires at least 3 electives from ANTH 220 FOOD AND CULTURE; ANTH 238 URBAN ANTHROPOLOGY; ANTH 314 CROSSING BORDERS: GROWING UP LATINX; an unnamed catalog entry; SOCI 203 SOCIOLOGY OF SPORT; SOCI 205 SOCIOLOGY OF AGING; SOCI 206 ENVIRONMENTAL SOCIOLOGY; SOCI 221 SOCIAL MOVEMENTS; SOCI 230 SOCIOLOGY OF HEALTH & MEDICINE; SOCI 232 SOCIOLOGY OF FAMILY; SOCI 260 SOCIOLOGY OF MEDIA AND POP CULTURE; SOCI 303 SOCIOLOGY OF CULTURE; SOCI 309 FOOD AND POPULATION; SOCI 331 SOCIOLOGY OF RELIGION; SOCI 335 PUBLIC SOCIOLOGIES. [1]

Career Pathways also requires PATH 001 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1, PATH 002 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 2, and PATH 003 CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 3. [1]

To identify what remains for you, review your Degree Audit (https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/) and make an appointment with your faculty academic advisor; see the scheduling slides if needed: https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/wp-content/uploads/sites/133/2026/02/How-to-Schedule-an-Appointment.pdf. [10]
Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7441. [10]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-BA-SOCI) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/)

question: what are the prereqs for the research methods course in psych, and do i need stats done first?

question: What gen ed requirements are there overall at Ramapo? I'm trying to figure out which categories I still have left to fill.

body.answer:
Ramapo’s published curriculum describes ten General Education courses [13]:
1. Four keystone courses: First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities. Critical Reading & Writing 102 must be taken within the first 64 credits [13].
2. One course in each of four keystone categories: Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits [13].
3. One course in two of three distribution categories: Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. At least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the school housing your major [13].
The catalog also lists the required courses as First-Year Seminar, Critical Reading and Writing II, Social Science Inquiry, and Studies in the Arts and Humanities, plus the four keystone categories and two distribution categories [1, 3]. It says reading/writing and mathematics must be completed by 64 credits; Banner can block schedule creation or adjustment if the requirements are unmet at that point [7, 8].
The distribution-category name differs across pages: section 6 calls one category “Social Systems and Society,” while sections 1 and 13 call it “Systems, Sustainability, and Society” [1, 6, 13]. Section 6 says choose two of the three categories; beginning Fall 2026, the “out of school requirement” is no longer enforced in degree audit tools [6].
I can’t verify which categories you personally still need. Review your Degree Audit, then make an appointment with your faculty academic advisor [9]: https://web.ramapo.edu/degree-audit-tools/. For help, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441, D-207.

Sources: [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/)

body.answer:

4. Select the current term and click enter, then click “Generate New Evaluation.”
5. Click the circle next to your major and click “Generate Request.”
6. Select detail requirements and click “Submit.”

After reviewing your Degree Audit, make an appointment with your faculty academic advisor to discuss remaining courses. [3,5] If you need help finding your advisor, review https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/wp-content/uploads/sites/133/2026/02/How-to-Schedule-an-Appointment.pdf. [3]

question: Should I do a double major in psych and sociology or just major in one and minor in the other? Which looks better for grad school?

body.answer:
The catalog lists Psychology BA and Sociology BA, but no bachelor's major named “psych sociology.” [15] Both Psychology and Sociology minors are also listed. [3][4] Ramapo says undergraduates may pursue a minor and/or second major. [5] For two majors, no more than half the courses may double-count, and you must complete all writing-intensive courses required for the second major. [6]

Ramapo’s major-choice guidance says to consider double-majoring or a major and minor, weigh the risks and costs, and use graduation plans to check what is feasible. [10] It does not recommend one option over the other. I don’t have verified information about which option looks better to graduate schools. For help weighing your academic plans, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441, D-207. [10] For graduate-school guidance, contact the Cahill Career Development Center: careercenter@ramapo.edu, Main Office (201) 684-7444. [13]

Sources: [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MN-PSYC) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SO-MN-SOCI) [5](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/careercenter/career-assessment/) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: does ramapo have a nursing major or is it only for ppl who already have an rn

body.answer:
Yes—Ramapo has nursing bachelor’s majors, and it isn’t only for people who already have an RN. The catalog lists Nursing Accelerated BSN, Nursing Generic BSN, and Nursing RN to BSN [14].

The Generic BSN is for students interested in becoming nurses [1]. The RN-to-BSN track is designed for registered nurses with an associate’s degree or nursing diploma [3]. The Accelerated BSN is for prospective students with a non-nursing bachelor’s degree or at least 60 credits from a regionally accredited institution [2].

These BSN programs also list Nursing MSN at another level [1][2][3].

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURA) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS) [14](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: what classes do u need for the business admin major

body.answer:
The catalog lists no bachelor’s major called “business admin.” [14] Its related bachelor’s majors named there are Healthcare Administration BS and International Business BA; Business Administration is listed as an MBA. [14]

If you mean the Management BS, its required courses/categories are: [1]
- Quantitative Reasoning: choose one of MATH 108, MATH 110, or MATH 121.
- ASB requirements: ACCT 221, ACCT 222, BADM 223, BADM 225, BADM 495, ECON 101, ECON 102, FINC 301, INFO 224, MGMT 302, MGMT 370, and MKTG 290.
- Choose one International Category course: ECON 323, ECON 325, HNRS 220, IBUS 321, IBUS 322, IBUS 326, IBUS 305, IBUS 335, IBUS 336, or IBUS 340.
- Choose one Ethics Category course: BADM 301, HNRS 325, or INFO 315.
- MGMT 340 and MGMT 410.
- Choose one experiential course: MGMT 401, MGMT 466, or MGMT 475.
- Choose three Leadership and Talent Management courses from the listed options in the catalog. [1]
- Complete PATH 001, PATH 002, and PATH 003. [1]

The Management BS 2026–2027 recommended plan lists semesters, courses and totals here: https://www.ramapo.edu/recommended-graduation-plan-2026/asb/ba-management/. [1] For help identifying the major you mean, contact the Anisfield School of Business: asb@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7379, (201) 684-7380 or (201) 684-7378; ASB-333. [1]

question: is bio 101 a prereq for anatomy and physiology or can i take a&p first semester

body.answer:
BIOL 101 is not listed as a prerequisite for BIOL 214, Anatomy and Physiology I Lecture. BIOL 214 has no published prerequisites [2]. BIOL 101 also has no published prerequisites [1]. So the published catalog information does not require BIOL 101 before BIOL 214. [1][2]

For registration, the Registrar says to “satisfactorily complete all prerequisites before registering,” and to review prerequisite requirements in Web Self Service and course descriptions there [3]. The course-prerequisites page says to select a subject to see class prerequisites [4]. These pages support taking BIOL 214 in your first semester if there are no other registration restrictions; the pages do not confirm your individual eligibility or course availability. Contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695 with registration questions. [3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL101) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL214) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/) [4](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/course-prerequisites/)

question: im an incoming freshman thinking about pre med, what should i take my first semester for the bio major

body.answer:
Assuming you mean Biology BS (the catalog also lists Biochemistry BS and Bioinformatics BS) [15]: the Biology: General Pre-Med Track plan for students admitted in 2026–2027 recommends this first-year Fall Semester (total 18 credits): BIOL 111 and BIOL 111L (4); CHEM 116 and CHEM 116L (4); CRWT 102 (4); INTD 101 (4). First Year Seminar is taken in the first semester. CRWT and MATH courses are determined by placement testing and should be taken following the sequence above. [1]

BIOL 111 is required for the Biology BS major, along with BIOL 111L. BIOL 111 is 4 credits and has no published prerequisites. It introduces biological science, covering cells and information coding and transmission, and surveys major animal, plant and fungi phyla. [1][2] Biology Minor is also published. [1]

First-year schedules are based on your declared major, and you must meet your academic advisor before registering. Center for Student Success advisors advise first-year students. Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441 to discuss your plan. [5][6]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/BIOL111) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/) [15](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs)

question: what are all the gen ed requirements i need to graduate, like how many categories are there

body.answer:
Ramapo students take ten General Education courses [3]: four keystone courses, one course in each of four keystone categories, and one course in two of three distribution categories [3].

- Keystone courses: First Year Seminar; Social Science Inquiry; Critical Reading & Writing 102 (within the first 64 credits); and Studies in the Arts & Humanities [3].
- Keystone categories: one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning. Quantitative Reasoning must be taken within the first 64 credits [3].
- Distribution categories: choose two of Culture & Creativity, Systems, Sustainability, & Society, and Values & Ethics. At least one course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major [3].

So, there are four keystone categories and three distribution categories; you take courses in all four keystone categories and two of the three distribution categories [3]. The catalog describes the distribution choice as “Systems, Sustainability, and Society” [2]; section 1 instead calls it “Social Systems and Society.” The Provost page lists the three as Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society, and says to select two [1].

Reading/writing and mathematics must be completed by 64 credit hours [9]. Transfer students may transfer or receive waivers for some or all requirements [8]; the listed waivers and remaining requirements for students with at least 48 credits are in section 4. See approved courses in the College Catalog: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/college-wide-programs/gened#general-education-categories-and-courses [5].

Sources: [1](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics)
